title: On the momentum of population growth
source_note: v5 seminal. Founding derivation of the population-momentum factor (ratio of ultimate to current size at NRR=1). Theory; seeds the JEL theory stream, not empirical recall.

title: Population momentum: its relation to the moments of replacement level fertility
source_note: Analytic relation between the momentum factor and the fertility path to replacement. Replaces an unresolvable 'Espenshade correspondence' candidate that failed the existence gate.

title: The Future of Population Growth: Alternative Paths to Equilibrium.
source_note: Early quantification of built-in growth from a young age structure.

title: Completing the Demographic Transition
source_note: v5 seminal. Decomposes future growth into momentum vs above-replacement fertility vs declining mortality. Outcome is population GROWTH -> borderline OFF_OUTCOME_POP; the momentum component is A.9's. Extract the component, not the growth total.

title: Europe's Population at a Turning Point
source_note: v5 seminal. NEGATIVE momentum from an aged structure (SDT). Science; outcome is population size -> OFF_OUTCOME_POP tension, extract the momentum/age-structure component.

title: Population momentum expresses population aging
source_note: Recasts momentum as an aging phenomenon; the bridge between the momentum reading and the age-composition reading of A.9.

title: Movement toward stability as a fundamental principle of population dynamics
source_note: Stable-population convergence, the formal basis of momentum.

title: Population Momentum Across the Demographic Transition
source_note: Momentum factor traced across transition stages; directly FDT/SDT-relevant.

title: Demography, Measuring and Modeling Population Processes
source_note: Canonical textbook. Standardization/decomposition and stable-population methodology. Theory/method, not an effect estimate.

title: Components of a Difference Between Two Rates*
source_note: Kitagawa decomposition: the rate-vs-composition method an empirical A.9 paper uses to split a CBR change. Method canon. (Das Gupta's 1993 user's manual did not resolve in OpenAlex and is noted in the log, not anchored.)
container: Journal of the American Statistical Association

title: Demographic Transition Patterns and Their Impact on the Age Structure
source_note: How the transition builds the age structure; the determinant side (context, cross-ref A.1).

title: Population dynamics in an age of declining fertility
source_note: Births/age-structure dynamics under sub-replacement fertility. OpenAlex metadata drifted (dates it 2009, source 'Archined'; true venue Genus ~1997) -- kept keyed on title+authors per the drifted-identifier rule.

title: On the Quantum and Tempo of Fertility
source_note: DECOY -> A.11. Tempo distortion of the period TFR. Must NOT route to A.9 (Wall 1). If a query pulls this into A.9's core, the cause axis is too loose.

title: The Effects of Changes in Mortality and Fertility on Age Composition
source_note: DECOY on the A.1/A.9 seam. Classic Coale result that fertility, not mortality, drives age composition -> determinant of A.9's exposure, context only.

title: The coming acceleration of global population ageing
source_note: DECOY -> OFF_OUTCOME_POP. Outcome is population ageing/size, not a birth rate (Wall 3). The largest expected off-cell class.

title: MATRIX POPULATION MODELS: CONSTRUCTION ANALYSIS AND INTERPRETATION
source_note: DECOY for the 'age structure' homonym. Age-structured models of NON-human populations (ecology/pop-genetics), the 32k-record contamination the frame probe flagged. OpenAlex's top match is the published review of Caswell's monograph; a real off-topic 'age structure' record either way. OFF_OTHER.

title: Are population issues mainstreamed into climate change policies and action in Nigeria? Evidence from a systematic review of national climate change documents
source_note: The ONLY type:review hit for ('population momentum' OR 'demographic momentum') AND fertility (count=1). Off-topic (climate-policy mainstreaming). Recorded so the audit shows channel 1 was worked and is empty -- no systematic review / meta-analysis of A.9 exists, because A.9 is an accounting identity, not an effect literature. Contributes zero empirical anchors.
